chunks: ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Faḍḍāl, from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad ibn Ḥakīm and Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī al-Ṣabbāḥ together, from Ibrāhīm ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd, from Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, who said:
“Do not touch the muṣḥaf without taharah, nor in a state of janabah, and do not touch its binding-thread, nor suspend it.
Indeed Allah, the Exalted, says: “None touch it except the purified ones.”

key_terms.جُنُبًا: a person in a state of janabah requiring ghusl
key_terms.ٱلْمُصْحَفُ: the written codex of the Qur'an

ai.seo_question: Can a person in janabah or without taharah touch the muṣḥaf?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling that the muṣḥaf must not be touched without ritual purity, especially by one in a state of janabah. It also cites the Qur'anic phrase «لَا يَمَسُّهُ إِلَّا ٱلْمُطَهَّرُونَ» as support for the sanctity and handling etiquette of the Qur'an.
